messages.text: What seed is good for southern Illinois?

For Illinois (including southern IL), these native milkweed species are generally good choices, depending on your site conditions:

Best all-around picks (widely adaptable in IL):

- Common milkweed (Asclepias syriaca), full sun, average to dry soils; very hardy and easy, spreads by rhizomes (best for larger areas).

- Swamp milkweed (Asclepias incarnata), full sun to part sun, moist to wet soils (rain gardens, ditches, low spots); clump-forming and well-behaved.

- Butterfly milkweed (Asclepias tuberosa), full sun, dry to well-drained soils (sandy/gravelly), drought tolerant; does not like wet feet.

Great for prairies and open, sunny sites:

- Whorled milkweed (Asclepias verticillata), full sun, dry to medium soils; more slender, good in prairies and edges.

- Prairie milkweed (Asclepias sullivantii), full sun, medium to moist prairie soils; very monarch-friendly (often sold as “Sullivant’s milkweed”).

- Poke milkweed (Asclepias exaltata), part shade, medium moisture; good for woodland margins.

We have all of them here: https://lasclay.com/en-us/collections/garden
